notes: PSA 7.3 ng/mL. PI-RADS 5. PSAD 0.11. Prostate volume 64 mL. csPCa 0.85.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management options following a repeat biopsy confirming persistent ISUP grade group 2 disease.

The patient is a 64-year-old office administrator with a known history of prostate cancer, initially diagnosed in 2022. He has been under urological follow-up since then. His PSA has fluctuated, with a recent rise to 7.3 ng/mL in January 2025. He reports severe lower urinary tract symptoms, with an IPSS score of 30/35, which significantly impacts his quality of life. He is married but lives alone, with his adult daughter acting as his primary contact for medical communications. He is an ex-smoker (30 pack-years, quit in 2003) and enjoys hiking on weekends. He consumes approximately 7 units of alcohol per week. His comorbidities include hypertension, managed with amlodipine, valsartan, and metoprolol. He recently attended a vascular surgery consultation for varicose veins and received his flu vaccination from the GP practice nurse.
On DRE, the prostate is non-palpable, consistent with a cT1c stage. General examination is unremarkable, with stable vital signs and no signs of acute distress.
